newsitem.title: POLAND: Nomura sees Polish 1996 inflation at 20 pct.
newsitem.headline: Nomura sees Polish 1996 inflation at 20 pct.

text.p: Year-on-year inflation in Poland should ease to 20 percent this year from 21.6 percent in 1995 and 16 percent in 1997, Nomura Equity Research said in the appendix to a report on insurer Warta SA.

The finance ministry predicts year-on-year inflation of 17 percent at the end of this year and 13 percent at the end of 1997. Over the first seven months of 1996, year-on-year inflation was 20.4 percent.
Nomura forecast a gross national product rise of 5.0 percent this year and 5.3 percent next year after 1995's 7.0 percent.
It said the discount rate should fall to 20 percent at the end of this year and to 17 percent at the end of next year from the current 22 percent.
Nomura also said the dollar should cost 2.9 zlotys at the end of this year and 3.2 zlotys at the end of next year against the current 2.75 zlotys.
